indicators.note: The archaic sense, as in 'without the city walls' — outside rather than lacking, so the comedian goes round what follows.

blocks.note: a gagster is a comedian, a trader in gags
n. is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.walkthrough: Everything turns on hearing 'without' as outside rather than lacking: the comedian keeps all his letters and merely opens up to admit one more.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough is a noun for a violent thug, and a gangster is the organised professional version — the definition names the type, the answer the trade.

clue.text: Just a second to remove top? Doubtful (4)

indicators.note: In a down entry the top is where the word begins, so this asks for the opening letter to go.

blocks.note: 'just a second' is a jiffy, the moment you ask someone to wait
the first letter of JIFFY sits at the top of a down entry, and it is the one that goes

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark earns its keep: it warns that the words before it are an instruction to the solver, not more of the plea to wait a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iffy is unreliable and not to be trusted, so 'Doubtful' is the dubious-quality sense rather than a person harbouring doubts.

blocks.note: taken at face value, straight off the page
the nub of a matter is its core
Is. is the map-maker's abbreviation for island
surface only: it paints the island scene and hands over no letters

explanation.walkthrough: Anubis is the jackal-headed Egyptian god of embalming and the dead, so 'god' alone is the definition and the sun belongs to the picture the surface paints.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the answer is one named deity and 'god' is the whole category, leaving the three small pieces to say which one.

clue.text: Depend on getting in support for a music genre (7)

indicators.note: It is an instruction to climb inside: the piece it follows ends up lodged within the piece it precedes.

blocks.note: a bra is a support, the crossword's favourite undergarment
to depend on something is to hang on it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Depend' comes from the Latin for hanging down, which is why the swap is so clean; the surface reads as leaning on somebody for a favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhangra is the Punjabi dance music that crossed into British pop, so the definition places it by category rather than describing its sound.

clue.text: Wizard at foot of elder tree (4)

indicators.note: The foot of a word is its end, so only the closing letter of the word beside it is wanted.

blocks.note: a wizard at something is an ace at it
the last letter of elder

explanation.walkthrough: Elder is itself a tree, which is the trap: it looks like the definition and is really just a word being asked for its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus of maples and sycamores, so 'tree' defines the answer by the class its Latin name belongs to.

clue.text: Fig, pear almost turn out to be the possible basis of fad diet (10)

indicators.note: Almost a word is that word one letter short, so the final letter never makes it into the mix.
Out of order is the sense here: what stands before it is not in the arrangement you need.

blocks.note: both fruits go into the mix whole, seven letters
TURN with its last letter clipped off by 'almost'

explanation.walkthrough: Three fruits in one clue and only two of them are letters; the third is what you are looking for, which is the whole misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The grapefruit diet was a real 1970s craze, so the definition reaches the answer through the fad rather than through botany.

clue.text: Chestnut one replaced with ring for crop protection (6)

indicators.note: It names a swap rather than a loss: one letter steps out and whatever comes after takes its seat.

blocks.note: an old chestnut is a cliche, a joke told once too often
one is I in Roman numerals, and it is the letter that leaves
a ring is drawn as the letter O, and it moves in

explanation.walkthrough: Chestnut looks horticultural in a clue about crops, and is not: the tired old joke is the sense the setter wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloche is the bell-shaped glass or plastic cover a gardener sets over young plants, so 'crop protection' describes it by the job it does.

blocks.note: Hal is Shakespeare's Prince Hal, the future Henry V
a finch is a bird

explanation.walkthrough: The (4-4) enumeration says two hyphenated halves, and the join falls inside the bird rather than between the two clue words.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-inch is Cockney rhyming slang for pinch, and to pinch a thing is to nick it, so the definition works through the rhyme.

indicators.note: A blunt cancellation: whatever it points at is struck out of the letters already assembled.

blocks.note: a corral is the pen cowboys drive cattle into
r is the standard abbreviation for right, and it is the letter dropped

explanation.walkthrough: Two exclamatory scraps that read as a rancher's grumble are really an instruction: keep the pen, lose one of its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral names the pinkish-orange colour of the sea creature's skeleton, so 'Pink' asks for a shade rather than the reef itself.

indicators.note: To articulate is to say something out clearly, so the word after it is wanted as a noise, not a spelling.

blocks.note: the ugli is a Jamaican citrus hybrid, and its name spoken aloud is what goes in the grid

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' is the old word for beautiful, so the definition has nothing to do with justice, which is exactly what the surface hopes you assume.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in its old sense means lovely to look at, so its negative is unlovely: the plain visual meaning, not unjust.

clue.text: Left and right wings of party turn back, collapsing into ruin (10)

indicators.note: The wings of a word are the letters at its two edges, and a party is the one thing that has a left and a right one.
A collapsing thing loses its shape, so the letters no longer hold the order they were handed to you in.

blocks.note: the outer letters of PARTY, the wings at its left and right
anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.walkthrough: The political surface does all the work: 'turn back' reads as an instruction to reverse something and is simply eight letters waiting to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin in the financial sense: the declared state of being unable to pay, which a court pronounces, rather than a general downfall.

clue.text: Hair loss ultimately comes before anxiety (6)

indicators.note: It points at the very end of the word beside it, so only that final letter is taken.
It fixes the order of the two pieces: the letter just taken goes in front, not behind.

blocks.note: the last letter of loss
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.walkthrough: Hair loss reads as one idea and is two pieces of machinery — and the answer is also a cause of it, which is the joke underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is the mental strain that 'anxiety' names in ordinary speech, not the engineer's load on a beam or the emphasis put on a syllable.

clue.text: Drugs defence involving college that’s associated with Houdini (10)

indicators.note: To involve something is to draw it in, so the letter it names joins the assembly rather than sitting outside it.

blocks.note: an E is an ecstasy tablet, so drugs in the plural are Es
c. is the standard abbreviation for college
an apology is a reasoned defence of a position, the sense in Newman's Apologia

explanation.walkthrough: The step that unlocks it is reading 'defence' as the older sense of apology, a justification rather than a regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapology is the stage art of getting out of chains and locked trunks, and Houdini is its most famous practitioner, so the art is named by its exemplar.

indicators.note: Beyond the dismissal, to sack a town is to ransack it, and what has been ransacked is left in complete disorder.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed word looks like a helpful gloss on 'fired' and is really the instruction, which is why it hides so well.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarefied air is thin air: the word describes a gas thinned out, and by extension a social circle too exclusive to breathe in.

clue.text: Stand for election (ironic) and get through all the booze (3,3)

blocks.note: in American usage a candidate runs for office where a Briton stands
dry humour is the ironic, deadpan sort

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is split between two lights, 15 and 17, which the (3,3) enumeration announces; 'stand' and 'run' are the British and American halves of one idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To run dry is for a supply to give out, so drinking a bar's stock to the last drop is the phrase happening in front of you.

blocks.note: P is the physicist's symbol for power
to recede is to decline, as a tide or a hairline goes back

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is joinery, not possession: read it as 'herald is power plus decline' and the clue falls open.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald a thing is to go in front of it and announce it: the answer is the plain verb of going first, without the fanfare.

clue.text: Hearing of pub expedition, neighbours start off (7)

indicators.note: It asks for the head of the word beside it, the single letter that word begins with.
Off means away rather than departing: the letter just named comes out of what has been built.

blocks.note: a pub is an inn
the first letter of neighbours, and the one the inn gives up
an expedition in search of something is a quest

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is village gossip about a pub outing, and the shortest word in it is the one carrying the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An inquest is the coroner's formal hearing into a sudden death, so 'Hearing' names it by the kind of legal proceeding it is.

clue.text: Game of kiss and tell, perhaps, with time for Latin (8)

indicators.note: It concedes that the words before it are only an approximate version of what you want, so their letters must be rearranged.
'X for Y' is the swap formula: what stands in front of it takes over the place of what stands behind.

blocks.note: both words hand over their letters, eight in all
L is the standard abbreviation for Latin, and it is the letter that leaves
t is the scientist's symbol for time, and it takes the L's place

explanation.walkthrough: A tabloid story and a Latin lesson make a plausible sentence, and neither survives the solve: the swap happens first, then the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittles is the pub game of bowling a ball at nine wooden pins, the ancestor of ten-pin bowling, so 'Game' defines it by category.

blocks.note: w. is the standard abbreviation for wife in a genealogy
a gang's enforcer is its hitman

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hands the poet a wife and a heavy; the apostrophe-s is joinery again, and the answer is a surname, which is how setters clue writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Whitman wrote Leaves of Grass, so 'Poet' defines by example: the class of person, with the surname alone standing for the man.

definitions.note: A triptych is one work made of three hinged panels, so the setter's plural names the parts while the answer names the whole thing.

indicators.note: Something damaged has been knocked out of shape, and letters knocked about no longer sit where they started.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.walkthrough: Both fodder words belong to rugby, which is what keeps 'damaged' reading as an injury report rather than an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A triptych is an altarpiece or picture painted on three hinged panels, so the definition points at it through the parts it is made of.

indicators.note: A lid is what sits on top, and in a down entry the top is where the word starts, so its first letter has gone.

blocks.note: a wringer squeezes the water out of washing before it dries
the W at the top of WRINGER is the lid that comes off

explanation.walkthrough: A dead ringer is an exact double, a sense that survives almost nowhere else; the surface offers a twin tub instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringer is a person or thing indistinguishable from another, the 'dead ringer' sense, so 'Twin' means look-alike rather than sibling.

blocks.note: a pat answer is a smooth one, delivered too readily
love is nothing in tennis, written as O
he lives = he is, the verb in its third person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Love lives' reads as a headline about romance and is two separate scraps of crosswordese stacked on top of each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A patois is the local vernacular of a region, often a creole one, so 'Dialect' is the plain word for the same kind of speech.

blocks.note: pi is short for pious, the crossword's word for devout
racy means risque, close to the bone

explanation.walkthrough: The two halves are opposites, piety and smut, which is the joke; 'and' does nothing but hold them together.
explanation.definitionFit: Buccaneering is robbery on the high seas and piracy is the noun for that trade, so the definition names the crime, not the criminal.

indicators.note: A fixed race is one arranged to somebody's liking, so these letters end up in an order somebody chose.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters

explanation.walkthrough: The (5-5) enumeration promises two hyphenated halves, and the surface, a child's hired bike being mended, could hardly look more innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankle-biter is Australian and British slang for a small child, low enough to bite you there, so 'Kid' is the everyday word for one.

blocks.note: this is the verb for the head-first shove a ram delivers
the target of everyone's mockery, the one a joke is aimed at, is described this way

explanation.walkthrough: Four words and no wordplay at all: the apostrophe-s poses as a possessive so the clue reads as a sentence about a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb for the head-first shove a ram gives, one noun for the target of mockery: the same word for the blow and the person taking it.

definitions.note: 'Bottle' is British slang for nerve and behaves as a singular, while the answer keeps a plural form for that same single quality.

blocks.note: bottle is British slang for nerve: losing your bottle is losing your courage
the essential inner workings of a machine, the parts that make it function, are described this way

explanation.walkthrough: Two everyday senses side by side with nothing joining them, which is what makes a four-word clue this hard to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage in slang, the nerve you either have or lose, and also the innards of a thing, the working parts without which it is a shell.

clue.text: Easy: massive return with little initially invested (4)

indicators.note: To return is to go back the way you came, so the word before it is read in the opposite direction.
It asks only for the letter a word starts with, the initial standing in for the whole.
Money invested is money put inside something, and the letter goes the same way.

blocks.note: massive = big, and 'return' turns those three letters round
the initial letter of little

explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy' is the trap: the answer means facile rather than effortless, the smoothness of a reply that came too readily to be thought about.
explanation.definitionFit: A glib answer is an easy one, fluent and unthinking, so 'Easy' catches the sense of too-ready smoothness rather than lack of difficulty.

clue.text: Crew strive to get leader replaced (5)

indicators.note: A word's leader is the letter at its front, and replacing it means a different letter takes that seat rather than the word simply losing one.

blocks.note: to strive for a cause is to fight for it
the F at the front of FIGHT is the letter turned out
the setter never names the incoming letter, so the definition is what fixes it as E

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a leadership challenge and the cryptic reading wants one at the head of a word. Only the definition says which letter moves in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight is the crew of eight oarsmen who row it, so the number stands for the whole boatload, a sense crosswords use constantly.

blocks.note: an arch look is a knowing, shrewd one
Charles Ives, the American composer of The Unanswered Question

explanation.walkthrough: 'Making records' reads as a session in a studio; the composer is here for his surname alone, which is how setters use famous people.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are the documents an institution keeps, so 'records' is the plain plural synonym, the stored papers rather than the act of recording.
